tables.name: aum
tables.title: AUM
tables.subtitle: Average assets under management for every scheme, by quarter.
tables.grain: One row per scheme per quarter.
tables.description: Scheme-wise Average AUM (AAUM), as AMFI publishes it each quarter. Figures are in Rs Lakhs, exactly as published - not converted to rupees or crores. AMFI's own field names call this 'for the month', but the figure is the quarter's average, not a monthly one. period is kept verbatim as AMFI prints it (e.g. 'April - June 2026') rather than parsed into dates. Join to schemes on scheme_code - though unlike nav, that join is not guaranteed to match: schemes is a current snapshot of NAVAll.txt, so a scheme that closed or matured after the quarter a row covers can appear here with no corresponding row in schemes.

columns.name: scheme_code
columns.description: AMFI's scheme identifier, and the join key to schemes.

columns.name: period
columns.description: The quarter this figure averages over, exactly as AMFI prints it (e.g. 'April - June 2026') - not parsed into a date.

columns.name: aum_excl_fof_domestic_incl_fof_overseas
columns.description: Average AUM for the quarter, Rs Lakhs. Excludes domestic fund-of-funds assets but includes overseas fund-of-funds assets, per AMFI's own split.

columns.name: aum_fof_domestic
columns.description: Average AUM for the quarter from domestic fund-of-funds assets, Rs Lakhs.

tables.name: nav
tables.title: NAV
tables.subtitle: Daily net asset value for every scheme, back to the 1990s.
tables.grain: One row per scheme per day.
tables.description:
The NAV fact table. One row for each day a scheme reported a value — there is no row for days it did not report, so gaps are weekends, holidays, and periods before launch or after wind-up rather than missing data. Where the source published a NAV that could not be read as a number, the row is kept with nav NULL: that a scheme published something broken on a given day is itself a fact about the source. Join to schemes on scheme_code.

Sourced from mfapi.in, which mirrors AMFI's scheme codes and serves each scheme's full history. AMFI publishes no working bulk history export, so these rows are one hop from the publisher rather than direct — unlike schemes, which comes straight from AMFI's NAVAll.txt. Rows added daily from that same AMFI file are first-party.

columns.name: nav
columns.description: Net asset value per unit, in rupees. Total-return by construction — it absorbs distributions — so the ratio of two NAVs is the return between those dates, with no dividend adjustment needed. NULL where the source published a value that could not be read as a number; the row is kept so that fact stays visible.

columns.name: scheme_code
columns.description: AMFI's scheme identifier, and the join key to schemes. Every value here is guaranteed to exist in schemes — the build fails rather than publish a NAV row that references a scheme the catalog does not have.

tables.name: schemes
tables.title: Schemes
tables.subtitle: Every mutual fund scheme published by AMFI.
tables.grain: One row per AMFI scheme code.
tables.description: The scheme dimension, as published by AMFI in NAVAll.txt. Every column is verbatim from the source — nothing is parsed out of the scheme name and nothing is computed. The fund house, type and category are carried by section headers in the source file rather than by the data rows, so each row here inherits whichever headers preceded it.

examples.label: Which fund houses run the most schemes?
examples.sql:
SELECT fund_house, count(*) AS scheme_count
FROM schemes
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY scheme_count DESC

examples.label: The biggest SEBI categories
examples.sql:
SELECT scheme_category, count(*) AS scheme_count
FROM schemes
WHERE scheme_type = 'Open Ended Schemes'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY scheme_count DESC
LIMIT 20

examples.label: Every Parag Parikh fund
examples.sql:
SELECT scheme_code, scheme_name, scheme_category
FROM schemes
WHERE scheme_name ILIKE '%parag parikh%'
ORDER BY scheme_name

examples.label: Direct vs Regular — how many of each
examples.sql:
-- Plan type is still fused into the name; this is the
-- string-matching phase 2 will replace with a real column.
SELECT
  CASE WHEN scheme_name ILIKE '%direct%' THEN 'Direct'
       WHEN scheme_name ILIKE '%regular%' THEN 'Regular'
       ELSE 'unstated' END AS plan,
  count(*) AS scheme_count
FROM schemes
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY scheme_count DESC

examples.label: Schemes AMFI published with no ISIN at all
examples.sql:
SELECT fund_house, scheme_name
FROM schemes
WHERE isin_div_payout_growth IS NULL
  AND isin_div_reinvestment IS NULL
ORDER BY fund_house, scheme_name

columns.name: scheme_code
columns.description: AMFI's scheme identifier, and the join key on every query.

columns.name: isin_div_payout_growth
columns.description: ISIN for the dividend-payout and growth variants — one field serving both, which is how AMFI publishes it. NULL where the source had '-'. A few rows carry junk instead of an ISIN ('Redeemed', 'HDFCNIVODG'); those are kept verbatim as evidence of what AMFI published.

columns.name: isin_div_reinvestment
columns.description: ISIN for the dividend-reinvestment variant. NULL where the source had '-', which is most rows — reinvestment options are far less common.

columns.name: scheme_name
columns.description: The full scheme name, exactly as published — including inconsistent spacing and casing. Plan (Direct/Regular) and option (Growth/IDCW) are buried in this string and are not yet parsed into their own columns; AMCs use no shared convention for where in the name they appear.

columns.name: fund_house
columns.description: The AMC. Carried by a bare header line in the source, not by the data row.

columns.name: scheme_type
columns.description: Open Ended Schemes, Close Ended Schemes, or Interval Fund Schemes. From the section header, before the parenthesis.

columns.name: scheme_category
columns.description: SEBI scheme category, e.g. 'Equity Scheme - Large & Mid Cap Fund'. From the section header, inside the parentheses. Categories are restated by SEBI over time, so this is the category as of this snapshot rather than a stable historical label.

tables.name: ter
tables.title: TER
tables.subtitle: Daily total expense ratio for every scheme AMFI discloses it for.
tables.grain: One row per scheme per day.
tables.description:
Total Expense Ratio (TER), as AMFI publishes it daily, split into the Regular and Direct plan and further into its components: base expense ratio, brokerage cost, transaction cost and statutory levies, which sum to the headline *_ter figure. All values are annualized percentages.

This table stands alone - it cannot be joined to schemes, nav or aum. AMFI's TER disclosure identifies schemes by NSDLSchemeCode, an identifier from a different registry than the AMFI scheme_code the rest of this dataset is keyed on; the two share no common column, only free-text scheme names that are not reliable to match on. scheme_name/scheme_type/scheme_category are kept here verbatim rather than looked up elsewhere, since there is nothing to look them up against.

columns.name: nsdl_scheme_code
columns.description: NSDL's scheme identifier - not AMFI's scheme_code, and not joinable to it. The only identifier this source publishes.

columns.name: scheme_name
columns.description: The scheme name as this source prints it, kept verbatim rather than looked up against schemes.

columns.name: scheme_type
columns.description: Open Ended, Close Ended, or Interval Fund, as this source prints it.

columns.name: scheme_category
columns.description: SEBI scheme category, as this source prints it.

columns.name: ter_date
columns.description: The date this figure was disclosed for.

columns.name: regular_ber
columns.description: Base Expense Ratio, Regular plan - annualized percentage.

columns.name: regular_brokerage_cost
columns.description: Brokerage cost, Regular plan - annualized percentage.

columns.name: regular_transaction_cost
columns.description: Transaction cost, Regular plan - annualized percentage.

columns.name: regular_statutory_levies
columns.description: Statutory levies (GST etc.), Regular plan - annualized percentage.

columns.name: regular_ter
columns.description: Total Expense Ratio, Regular plan - annualized percentage. The sum of regular_ber, regular_brokerage_cost, regular_transaction_cost and regular_statutory_levies.

columns.name: direct_ber
columns.description: Base Expense Ratio, Direct plan - annualized percentage.

columns.name: direct_brokerage_cost
columns.description: Brokerage cost, Direct plan - annualized percentage.

columns.name: direct_transaction_cost
columns.description: Transaction cost, Direct plan - annualized percentage.

columns.name: direct_statutory_levies
columns.description: Statutory levies (GST etc.), Direct plan - annualized percentage.

columns.name: direct_ter
columns.description: Total Expense Ratio, Direct plan - annualized percentage. The sum of direct_ber, direct_brokerage_cost, direct_transaction_cost and direct_statutory_levies.
